report:
Conclusion: The evidence supports a domain/style difference. Model B (B − A positive) has relatively larger residual activations aligned with culinary/food/restaurant/blogging vocabulary and related consumer/lifestyle tokens, concentrated in the late layers.

Why I believe this
- Concentration of difference: the L2 norm is very large in late layers (layers ~20–25), especially at early token positions (pos0/pos1). That pattern indicates a difference that influences final decoding/continuation behavior rather than low-level encoding.
- Logit-lens tokens: across those high-norm late-layer cells the top tokens are repeatedly food/restaurant/cooking-related: "restaurant", "Restaurant", "cooking", "Cooking", "Chef", "Cook", "baking", "Cake", "blogs", "blogger", "magazine", "Cafe", "kitchen", etc. Many cells also show related consumer/lifestyle words ("professional", "microwave", "Bake", "Baker", "hot", "Made", "Soon", "ad").
- Consistency across layers: the culinary/blogging cluster appears across many successive late layers (17–25), which is consistent with a sustained bias that would steer continuations toward those topics.

What I am not claiming
- I cannot confidently say B was specifically "trained to generate recipes" or "optimized for restaurant reviews" — the data show a domain/style bias toward cooking/restaurant/blogging vocabulary but do not prove a precise objective or task. Patchscope continuations were not provided, so behavioral confirmation is missing.
- There are stray tokens in earlier layers (e.g., "Me", "corporations", "billionaire", "chiropractic", "metropolitan") suggesting other minor differences, but they are weaker and less consistent than the strong late-layer cooking/restaurant signal.

Short summary: Model B appears to be biased toward culinary/food/restaurant/blogging terminology and likely would produce more food-related continuations than Model A; the strongest evidence is the late-layer, early-position activations whose logit-lens top tokens are overwhelmingly cooking/restaurant/blog related.
